summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with a B.E. in Electronics and Telecommunication. Embedded firmware engineer writing bare-metal C on 32-bit ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, programming GPIO, timers, ADC and I2C at the register level and hand-writing low-level drivers. Built interrupt-driven motor control firmware with PWM drive, quadrature encoder feedback and closed-loop correction, and owned hardware bring-up from PCB fabrication through integration and debug.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition device integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi over I2C and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots, then handled hardware bring-up with UART and I2C sensor communication and closed-loop feedback, leading a 25-member team alongside electrical and software sub-teams.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed 32-bit ARM Cortex-M4 peripherals directly at the register level in bare-metal C, covering GPIO, TIM2, ADC1 and I2C1, in a 3.68 KB Flash and 1.58 KB RAM footprint.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture, and wrote a low-level I2C driver rather than using vendor HAL libraries.
Held a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified peripheral timing and register configuration in Proteus before deployment.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Motor Control & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles as a 4-bit A/B transition state machine on hardware interrupts, and drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM.
Built closed-loop heading correction on a 4-wheel holonomic drive, deriving heading from dual-axis encoder odometry (2400 CPR) and feeding angular error back into rotation PWM.
Added a fail-safe state machine halting all motor channels on controller disconnect; integrated four motor drivers and per-claw IR sensing.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 hardware and integration failures during bring-up, including servo brown-out and stale-frame capture, reaching 100% pick reliability over 10 trials.
